question: Why did iZotope build Nectar 5 around software that reads a vocal's words and listens to its sound?

rungs.question: Why let a producer put an effect on a single word by selecting it in a transcript?
rungs.answer: Effects on one word or one line usually mean drawing automation, often across several plug-ins, which iZotope says can take an hour. Selecting the word as text replaces that step.

evidence.quote: They're also the ones that tend to take an hour of automation tweaking.
it’s a fast and intuitive way to spice up a vocal with effects without getting into the weeds with automation across multiple plugins

counter.text: iZotope's own documentation says the transcript can be wrong and needs fixing by hand: "Transcription won’t always spell every word the way you would, especially in a sung vocal." (docs.izotope.com, 2026-11-17). Scope: the five given pages only.

rungs.question: Why can a plug-in work from the words of a whole take at all?
rungs.answer: Moments runs through ARA, which lets it read the whole audio clip on the timeline rather than only the sound playing at that moment. It transcribes that clip on the producer's own computer and links each word to its place in time.

evidence.quote: Moments is an ARA plugin, meaning that it can edit audio on the timeline directly, rather than working on a stream of real-time audio that’s coming in through the DAW’s playback.
Moments works on audio clips through ARA, which lets it read the whole clip, not just the audio playing at the moment.

counter.text: It only works where the DAW supports ARA, with limits: "in Logic Pro, ARA currently runs on Intel or under Rosetta only, and in REAPER, ARA works in the VST3 format." (izotope.com, 2026-11-23). Loaded as an ordinary effect, the docs say Moments "can’t hear your audio". Scope: the five given pages only.

rungs.mechanism_type: technical protocol (ARA clip access plus on-device transcription)

rungs.question: Why does the Vocal Assistant listen to the vocal before building a chain?
rungs.answer: It listens to a stretch of the vocal, eight seconds by default, to learn its tone and dynamics, then sets up a whole processing chain aimed at a target for that style or a reference. iZotope frames the result as a fast starting point the producer then adjusts.

evidence.quote: This AI-powered mixing tool listens to a portion of your vocal and designs a customized processing chain to match it.
Trained on pro vocal standards, it gives you a tailored starting point in seconds, so you can spend your time dialing in your own sound.

counter.text: iZotope added a manual Custom Flow because the one-click result is not always where a producer wants to land: "But sometimes you already know where you want to end up." (izotope.com, 2026-11-23). What "pro vocal standards" means is not stated on any given page. Scope: the five given pages only.

rungs.mechanism_type: the model (listen, analyse, set a chain toward a target)

rungs.question: Why make these tools the headline of a paid release?
rungs.answer: Nectar 5 sells at $179 until 7 December, then $249, with upgrade prices for existing owners. Moments comes only in full Nectar 5, not the cheaper Elements tier. The pages show the price and the tier split, not iZotope's reasons for drawing the line there.

evidence.quote: iZotope Nectar 5 is available now at an introductory price of $179 as part of its Cyber Season sale through December 7, after which it’ll cost $249. Upgrade and crossgrade pricing is available.
Everything in Elements, plus 12 full modules and 2 mini-modules, 14 component plugins, Moments, Breath Control, and Melodyne 5 essential

counter.text: MusicRadar does not mention the Elements tier, so the tier split rests on iZotope alone. No source states why Moments was kept out of Elements. Scope: the five given pages only.

landing.shows: The sources show how the two tools work: Moments uses ARA to read a whole take, transcribes it on the producer's computer and ties effects to words, replacing automation that iZotope says can take an hour; Vocal Assistant listens for a few seconds and sets a full chain as a starting point. They show the price and that Moments sits only in the higher tier, but not why iZotope split it that way.
landing.open_question: When a plug-in can find every word in a take as text, what part of a vocal producer's job is still done by ear?
